description.narrative: The project will support the development of livestock value chains by increasing the outreach of participating financial institutions (PFIs) to livestock farmers and entrepreneurs throughout the country. It will improve access to market-based, long-term finance for producers, processing enterprises, input suppliers, and service providers in the livestock value chain. The project will help increase livestock productivity, sustainability, processing capacity and utilization; as well as marketing of inputs and livestock products.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Access to finance in the livestock subsector increased. Indicator: 725 sub-loans extended to livestock producers and value chain enterprises (2019 baseline: not applicable) Achievement: 48 Progress/Status: As of 1 July 2025, there were 649 subprojects financed by 6 PFIs. Data Source: PFI quarterly and annual progress reports; and quarterly and annual project monitoring reports by PMO

Output: Access to finance in the livestock subsector increased. Indicator: At least 5% of sub-loans extended to livestock producers and agribusiness enterprises led by women (2019 baseline: 0) Achievement: 10.78 Progress/Status: Achieved. As of 1 July 2025, the number of subloans extended to livestock producers and agribusiness enterprises led by women is 70 women (10.78%) Data Source: PFI quarterly and annual progress reports; and quarterly and annual project monitoring reports by PMO

Output: Access to finance in the livestock subsector increased. Indicator: At least two training sessions on preparing sub-loan documentation conducted by each PFI for potential sub-borrowers Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Achieved. - JSCM “Ipoteka bank” organized 2 offline trainings in December 2021 and in January 2022 which covered overall 70 participants, of which 23 (33%) participants were women. The speakers were the head of credit line - S.Samadov and a credit line specialist - Z.Abduraimov. - JSC “Mikrokredit bank” conducted 2 online trainings in December 2021 which covered overall 60 participants, of which 18 (30%) participants were women. The speaker was A.Nosirov - the credit line specialist. - JSC “Qishlok Qurilish Bank” conducted 2 online trainings in January 2022 which covered overall 100 participants, of which 40 (40%) participants were women. The speaker was A.Ametova - the credit line specialist. - JSC “Turon Bank” conducted 2 online trainings in January 2022 which covered overall 62 participants, of which 20 (32%) participants were women. - JSC “Halk Bank” conducted 2 online trainings in February 2022 which covered overall 116 participants, of which 51 (44%) participants were women. Speaker was a credit line specialist A.Karimov. - JSC “Uzbek Industrial and Construction Bank” conducted 2 trainings in April 2022 which covered overall 62 participants, of which 19 (31%) participants were women.
- The PIU Gender specialist participated in all trainings so that PFI branch staff and subborrowers would be familiarized with the information regarding the Project GAP implementation on a regular basis.
Data Source: PFI quarterly and annual progress reports; and quarterly and annual project monitoring reports by PMO
